name: Mahlon D. Ogden's house, Washington Square

function.note: The home of Mahlon D. Ogden (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759), brother of William B. Ogden (p. 627).

built.note: When it was built is not found: reconstructed as before the war.

research_note: MAHLON D. OGDEN'S HOUSE, built by T-3689 for the 1871 scene: the house in the burnt North Side that the fire famously spared (Andreas notes it was not the only one), a two-storey frame house in its own grounds facing Washington Square, the block of Clark, Dearborn, Oak and Washington Square streets. 'The building was of wood, surrounded by a wooden fence'; with the family away, friends saved it with blankets and carpets wetted from the hydrants and then the cistern while the fire passed (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759). Read off Melander & Henderson's stereograph No. 51.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire, which it survived; the phase ends with the scene.

position.symbolic_location: Washington Square's north side, the block between Clark and Dearborn Streets (today the Newberry Library's site).
position.note: Mid-block on the 1871 plan's block between Clark and Dearborn Streets, its front to Washington Square, set back about 18 m behind the north walk in its grounds. Andreas (vol. 2, p. 759) and Conzen's map (plate C2) place it on the block; the set-back and the place along the front are reconstructed. The footprint's origin is local E 612.4 N 1474.93.

derivation.reason: Set on the 1871 plan's block from the texts; no traced frontage for the 1871 city is in data/traces/street_control.json.

footprint.note: About fifty by forty feet, read off the stereograph's five-bay front; the depth is reconstructed.

fire.note: 'M. D. Ogden's house had escaped, and stood in almost perfect order, surrounded by large elm trees' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 754). 'The fence and barn took fire. Blankets and carpets were spread over the exposed places', wetted from the hydrants and then from the cistern on the premises (p. 759).

blocks.name: the house
blocks.note: A two-storey frame house of wood (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759) with a bracketed cornice and a low hip roof, five bays across its front, as Melander & Henderson's stereograph shows it through the elms; its depth and side windows are reconstructed.

porches.note: The veranda across the front, on posts, as the stereograph shows it.

value.note: Read off Melander & Henderson's stereograph No. 51 of the house just after the fire, and Andreas's account of how it escaped.

composition.note: Storeys, bays, veranda, cornice and roof from the stereograph; sizes reconstructed from it; the colour of the paint is not known and is built a pale stone colour.

wall_material.note: 'The building was of wood' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759).

phases.change_note: Built T-3689 (2026-11-20): the Ogden house stands in the 1871 scene on the landmark_1871 archetype.
